text.p: Following are the mein stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.

- Head of Osijek-Baranja county, Branimir Glavas refuses to transfer wheat to state reserves accusing government of corruption and smuggling wheat across the border only to import it again at higher prices.
- Rijeka court slaps Novi List daily with 59,000 kuna fine for allleged slander against the minister in the government Zeljko Luzavec.
- As stock market grows, buying shares seems to be the most lucrative business in the country. Traders said some are selling cars and real-estate to buy shares hoping for fast profits.
- Dresdener Bank Luxembourg to extend to Croatia a 200 million German marks loan for a two-year period. The loan should be used to cover the government's budget needs.
- Director of nonexistent British overseas Trading Company, which took advances offering well payed season jobs abroad, flees after accusations in the main daily.
- Polls show that most Zagrebians want the square named after late president of Yugoslavia Tito, renaimed into Teather square.
- Parliament attacks government's report on individual responsability for illegal spendings of the budget funds as insufficient. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
